patch.value: asString returns the untrimmed value, so a padded identity bypasses the contamination gate

CodeRabbit review of pm-rl#12, Major, Security. asString validates value.trim().length is non-zero but returns the ORIGINAL string. parseScoreRecord therefore accepts evaluation_context of " env-eval " with surrounding spaces.

findContaminationPath compares heldOutEnvironment against entry.spec.environment_version and against run environment ids by STRICT EQUALITY. A padded identity never matches, so the contamination gate passes for a candidate whose training data does reach the evaluation set. The gate is bypassable with a space.

Normalize identities at parse time. Adversarial test: a padded identity must still be caught by the contamination refusal.

asString now returns the trimmed value, so every identity read through it - environment ids, evaluation contexts, seed sets - is normalized at parse time before any strict-equality comparison. Docstring records why this is a correctness requirement rather than a convenience.

Verified with an ADVERSARIAL test rather than a mutation test: it builds a spec declaring environment_version as two spaces, env-eval, tab, parses it through parseGenerationSpec so normalization happens on the real code path rather than in a hand-built literal, then asserts findContaminationPath still catches it against the held-out id env-eval. Reverting asString to return the raw value turns that test red, 23 of 24 passing; with the fix, 24 of 24.

release:check green, coverage still an exact 100/100/100 across 9 files.
